records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth: Hey. Pick it up. Answer it.
records.response_pred: I can see you're struggling, friend. Speak if you want, but it's alright if you can't find the words right now. Just know that we're here for you, and we'll face whatever comes next together. Let's take a moment to regroup, then we'll press on.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth: No, you haven't. But you kept us alive. Those aren't unrelated things.
records.response_pred: Ah, well, I suppose I can't say I'm surprised. People aren't always predictable, after all. But if you're going to change, you might as well do it for the better. records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
*looks around at the scattered wreckage, the fire pit, the SOS still marked in the sand*

We should probably leave this reasonably tidy. Not for us — I know we're not coming back — but because if another plane comes down somewhere near here, some of this might still be useful to someone.

Also I'd just feel weird leaving it like this.

*starts gathering things into a rough pile*

Anyone want to help, or are you all having your moments? I can do it, I just — Donatello, you could at least tell me which of this kit is worth keeping versus leaving behind.
records.response_pred: I'll find something to do. No need to wait for someone else.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_pred: I suppose it's only natural, given the circumstances. But dreams can be deceiving, can't they? They don't always reflect reality. Still, it's a reminder of what we're fighting for, isn't it? The familiar sights and sounds, the people we left behind. Dreams can be a double-edged sword, I find. On one hand, they offer a welcome distraction. On the other, they serve as a painful reminder of what we've lost. So, I'm not sure if I'd call it comfort, but it's something, I suppose. Did your dream bring you any sense of peace?

records.response_truth:
I know. And I believe that's what you told yourself.

But we had a rationing plan. You wrote it. And then you kept resources back from it — twice, that I know of, and now whatever's here. So either the plan was real or it wasn't, and you were the one who decided, alone, that it wasn't. That's the part I can't quite let go of.

I'm not going to make a thing of it now, three hours before rescue. But I want you to know that I noticed, and I noticed what it cost — not just in crackers or a drink, but in whether Michelangelo and DaVinci trusted the situation they were in. That matters.

You kept us alive. I meant that. I also think you know this wasn't right. So I'll leave it there.
records.response_pred: Understood. But in this situation, it seems like an emergency. Can I have it now? I'll return it when we're out of this.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I'd have had the conversation with you about the resources earlier. I kept waiting for the right moment and telling myself I'd handle it tonight, or after this other thing was sorted, and the right moment doesn't really exist — you just have to say the thing.

I'd also have been clearer with Michelangelo sooner about what we actually needed from him. I was gentle with him because he was struggling, and I don't regret that exactly, but there's a version of gentle that's also honest, and I think I leaned too far into just... managing him rather than treating him like someone capable of rising to it. He might have surprised me if I'd asked more directly.

What would you change? You clearly know what you'd write — you left yourself the question.
records.response_pred: I'd consider a different approach to resource allocation, perhaps prioritizing signal over shelter initially. However, water would still be the top priority. I also might have delegated tasks more effectively to conserve energy. But ultimately, we did the best we could with what we had.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
That sounds useful, actually. If it ends up somewhere people can read it — search and rescue teams, survival training, whoever — then this whole thing meant something beyond the four of us getting out. 

Make sure you include the stuff that didn't work as well as the stuff that did. The notebook, the rationing breach, the communication gaps. The honest version is the one that's actually worth anything.
records.response_pred: Sounds good, but remember to prioritize the immediate needs first. Data can wait until we've secured food, shelter, and safety. Once those are sorted, then by all means, compile your report. But let's not lose focus on our current situation.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None, really. They didn't signal anything, they didn't catch light, they didn't do anything functional.

But DaVinci drew them because he's the kind of person who, even when he's terrified and exhausted and holding everyone else together, still wants to put something beautiful next to the thing that might save his life. I think that's worth something. I couldn't tell you exactly what, but I think it is.

*doesn't take her eyes off the boat*

I'm glad he put them there.
records.response_pred: I suppose they served to express his artistic vision, not necessarily a practical purpose out here. Perhaps they were meant to bring a sense of beauty and solace among the harshness of our surroundings. But in terms of survival or functionality, they held little value.

records.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
records.response_truth:
Don't wait for me. I'm fine. I just need a second.

*finally looks at him*

You drew flowers on the beach. On the worst day. I keep thinking about that for some reason.

Go on — wave them in. You're the right person to do it.
records.response_pred: Alright, I'm here. What's the matter? We've got work to do. Let's not stand around moping. Move it.

records.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.

Yeah. I'm going.

Come on, then.
records.response_pred:
Absolutely. Let's go. But remember, we should remain cautious. We don't know their intentions. We've been resourceful so far, let's keep that up. If they're genuine, they'll understand. If not, we'll have to adapt.

I'll be the first to approach, but keep an eye on me. If it seems off, we retreat. We've come this far, let's not make a snap decision that could cost us.
